page: OVHcloud b2-120-flex is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. The underlying compute infrastructure is powered by 2.0 GHz Intel Haswell processors without TSX support. Memory capacity is allocated at 120.0 GB, providing an even ratio of 3.75 GB per core. The server includes 50 GB of local SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps, operating on a KVM hypervisor without dedicated hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reflects performance characteristics typical of older CPU architectures. Single-thread execution is modest, ranking in the lower percentiles across stress-ng single-core tests (1050.09) and Geekbench single-core scores (1087.0). However, parallel execution leverages the full 32-core allocation effectively, reaching 27173.71 in stress-ng multi-core tests, a PassMark CPU score of 28944.02, and strong throughput in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 210.12 GB/sec. Memory read bandwidth registers at 60.23 GB/sec on uncached blocks, though uncached write speeds fall back to 23.97 GB/sec.

The primary engineering tradeoff of the b2-120-flex is its reliance on high core count rather than high single-core clock frequencies or contemporary instruction sets like AVX-512. While its local SSD storage allocation is relatively compact at 50 GB, its 10 Gbps network bandwidth and high parallel capacity make it balanced for horizontally scaled microservices, multi-threaded batch compilation, static web delivery, and mid-tier in-memory caching layers.
description: OVHcloud b2-120-flex is a general-purpose instance featuring 32 dedicated x86_64 cores operating at 2.0 GHz on an Intel Haswell architecture. Paired with 120.0 GB of system memory, 50 GB of local SSD storage, and a 10 Gbps network baseline, the server delivers balanced multi-threaded compute without dedicated graphics acceleration. Benchmark metrics highlight modest single-thread performance offset by capable multi-core output, evidenced by an 8738.0 Geekbench multi-core score and strong multi-threaded compression metrics. Memory write throughput on large blocks is limited to 23.97 GB/sec, while read speeds reach 60.23 GB/sec. This configuration offers practical resource density for workloads demanding broad core parallelization and high network throughput, such as multi-threaded code compilation, distributed cache nodes, static web serving, and background ETL processing.
